newsitem.title: UK: NWE FUEL BARGES EASE WITH LOADING DELAYS SAID OVER.
newsitem.headline: NWE FUEL BARGES EASE WITH LOADING DELAYS SAID OVER.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges eased early on Thursday with some traders saying the move was prompted by the end of loading delays at two key sites, while others pegged it to a pricing game.
High sulphur barges traded a number of times at $94 a tonne fob ARA, compared with Wednesday's lowest trade level of $94.25-$95 a tonne. The best sellers were said to be at $95 by midday.
Some traders said downward pressure came in after loading delays were solved at two independent European storage sites but others said there was still a shortage of prompt supplies.
One market player, a major, was said to be keen on driving prices down.
A supplier said prompt was still short, adding that only material loading after August 11 could be found easily.
After the early morning trades, sellers suddenly disappeared from the market on news that a major refiner will be a buyer.

"Sellers disappeared as they learnt that a major may be a buyer, so they will wait for better prices. You can get $94 from a lot of people but with that buyer in, they think the market will go higher," one trader said.
Russian high sulphur cracked and straight-run cargoes were still offered at very strong numbers but no serious bids were coming in, traders said.

"I had an offer today for a cracked M-100 at two means plus $4, a pretty strong price," one trader said. "For straight-run I'm still hearing offers of mean, mean plus $7 but I don't see the bids against them."
